title: Flamingo and Gated Cross-Attention for Few-Shot VLMs

questions.question: New visual conditioning must not degrade a working language model on day one. What start state guarantees that?
options: Full visual influence immediately
Random gating per token
No language model at all
Gate closed: pure text until training opens it
questions.explanation: Closed gates preserve the base. This lesson conditions vision through trainable gates.

questions.question: What output shape does perceiver_resampler produce for 900 patches and num_latents=8?
options: 900 latents, because the resampler preserves every patch
8 latents, with the same feature dimension as the input patches
72 latents, because each patch contributes to eight blocks
A scalar, because the cross-attention is pooled globally
questions.explanation: The function initializes eight latent vectors and repeatedly updates them by attending to the patch list. The input length changes, but the latent count stays eight.

questions.question: For ['IMG0','t0','IMG1','t1'], which image may text token t1 attend to under interleaved_mask?
options: IMG0 only, because all images share one causal prefix
Both IMG0 and IMG1, because image tokens are never masked
IMG1 only, because it is the most recent preceding image
Neither image, because text-to-image attention is disabled
questions.explanation: interleaved_mask selects the last image position before each text position. t1 follows IMG1, so its row allows IMG1 and blocks the older IMG0.

questions.question: Which equation does gated_cross_attention_step implement?
options: y = cross / tanh(alpha), with no text residual
y = text_hidden - cross, independent of alpha
y = softmax(text_hidden) + cross
y = text_hidden + tanh(alpha) * cross_attention(text_hidden, visual_tokens)
questions.explanation: The helper computes cross-attention, scales it by math.tanh(alpha), and adds it to each text vector. The residual preserves the language stream while the gate opens.

questions.question: Which ordering matches Flamingo's few-shot interleaved prompt described in the lesson?
options: Three image-caption examples, then a query image whose caption is to be generated
Three captions with no images, then an image classification label
One image repeated three times, then an unrelated text-only prompt
A query image first, followed by captions that explain the answer
questions.explanation: Flamingo uses in-context multimodal examples: image and caption pairs precede a new image. The model must continue the pattern without a gradient update.

questions.question: What is approximately true of the visual contribution when alpha=2.0?
options: tanh(2)=0, so the text stream is unchanged
tanh(2) is about 0.96, so the cross-attention residual is mostly open
The gate becomes negative and subtracts visual features
The gate is clipped to exactly 2.0 before the residual is added
questions.explanation: math.tanh(2) is approximately 0.964. Compared with alpha=0, the visual residual therefore contributes strongly while the original text representation remains in the sum.
